Assess risk and report to user, echoing repo/worktree/index identity\n```\n\n> If \"Index is stale\" → run `node .gitnexus/run.cjs analyze` in terminal.\n> If `.gitnexus/run.cjs` is missing, replace `node .gitnexus/run.cjs` with `npx gitnexus` in the fallback commands.\n\n## Checklist\n\n```\n- [ ] list_repos {} — bind repo; explicit repo when >1 indexed, ask if ambiguous\n- [ ] impact({target, direction: \"upstream\"}) or CLI fallback to find dependents\n- [ ] Review d=1 items first (these WILL BREAK)\n- [ ] Check high-confidence (>0.8) dependencies\n- [ ] READ processes to check affected execution flows\n- [ ] detect_changes({scope: \"all\"}) or CLI fallback for pre-commit check\n- [ ] Confirm the checkout you edited is the checkout that was diffed\n- [ ] Assess risk level and report, stating repo/worktree/index identity\n```\n\n## Understanding Output\n\n| Depth | Risk Level       | Meaning                  |\n| ----- | ---------------- | ------------------------ |\n| d=1   | **WILL BREAK**   | Direct callers/importers |\n| d=2   | LIKELY AFFECTED  | Indirect dependencies    |\n| d=3   | MAY NEED TESTING | Transitive effects       |\n\n## Risk Assessment\n\n| Affected                       | Risk     |\n| ------------------------------ | -------- |\n| <5 symbols, few processes      | LOW      |\n| 5-15 symbols, 2-5 processes    | MEDIUM   |\n| >15 symbols or many processes  | HIGH     |\n| Critical path (auth, payments) | CRITICAL |\n| **Zero callers found**         | **UNKNOWN** |\n\n`UNKNOWN` is not a low rung on this scale — it means the walk could not answer.\nAn empty caller set is equally consistent with \"genuinely unused\" and \"the\ncallers are not resolvable by the index\" (plain-object property access, dynamic\ndispatch, cross-language calls), so few-callers ⇒ LOW does **not** apply. The\nresult carries a `riskNote` saying so. Confirm with a text search before\ntreating the symbol as safe to change or delete.\n\n`risk` is the edit gate: warn on HIGH/CRITICAL and stop on UNKNOWN until the\nuncertainty is resolved. Within single-repo mode, compare File and symbol\ntargets with local `riskSharedAxes` (direct/total only). Within group mode,\ncompare only group results: their `riskSharedAxes` overlays resolved\ncross-repo crossings on that local value. Never use either field to waive the\nedit gate. Check `riskScale.unusedAxes` before comparing kinds: MCP File walks\nomit process/module axes, while web Graph-RAG expands File targets to in-file\nsymbols before enrichment.\n\n## Tools\n\n**impact** — the primary tool for symbol blast radius. If MCP is unavailable, use `node .gitnexus/run.cjs impact <symbol> --direction upstream --repo .` instead:\n\n```\nimpact({\n  target: \"validateUser\",\n  repo: \"my-app\",          // required once >1 repository is indexed\n  direction: \"upstream\",\n  minConfidence: 0.8,\n  maxDepth: 3\n})\n\n→ d=1 (WILL BREAK):\n  - loginHandler (src/auth/login.ts:42) [CALLS, 100%]\n  - apiMiddleware (src/api/middleware.ts:15) [CALLS, 100%]\n\n→ d=2 (LIKELY AFFECTED):\n  - authRouter (src/routes/auth.ts:22) [CALLS, 95%]\n```\n\n**detect_changes** — git-diff based impact analysis. If MCP is unavailable, use `node .gitnexus/run.cjs detect-changes --scope all --repo .` instead:\n\n```\ndetect_changes({scope: \"all\"})\n\n→ Changed: 5 symbols in 3 files\n→ Affected: LoginFlow, TokenRefresh, APIMiddlewarePipeline\n→ Risk: MEDIUM\n```\n\nAdd `repo` once more than one repository is indexed, and `worktree: \"<abs\npath>\"` when your changes are in a linked worktree the server was not launched\nfrom.\n\n`partial: true` (a graph query failed) or `truncated: true` (the changed-symbol\nlisting was capped) means the result is short of the truth, and reads like\n`UNKNOWN` above: a zero there means unseen, not unaffected. READ gitnexus://repo/my-app/processes\n   → LoginFlow and TokenRefresh touch validateUser\n\n3. L90: # Conditional Routing
L91: 
L92: This feature is available on all Portkey 【45†plans】.
L93: 
L94: Using Portkey Gateway, you can route your requests to different provider targets based on custom conditions you define. These can be conditions like:
L95:   * If this user is on the `paid plan`, route their request to a `custom fine-tuned model`
L96:   * If the model parameter is set to `fastest`, route to `gpt-4o-mini`, if `smartest`, route to `openai o1`
L97:   * If this user is an `EU resident`, call an `EU hosted model`
L98:   * If the `temperature` parameter is above `0.7`, route to a more creative model
L99:   * If the request is coming from `testing environment` with a `llm-pass-through` flag, route it to the `cheapest model`
L100:   * ..and more!
L101: Using this strategy, you can set up sophisticated routing logic based on:
L102:   1. Metadata - Custom key-value pairs you pass with your requests
L103:   2. Request Parameters - Any parameter that you send in your original LLM request (like model, temperature, max_tokens)
L104:   3. Request URL Path - Match against `url.pathname` (for example, route `/v1/embeddings` requests)
L105: All routing happens very fast on the gateway, on edge.
L106: ##
L107: 
L108: 【46†​】
L109: 
L110: Enabling Conditional Routing
L111: 
L112: Conditional routing is one of the strategies in Portkey’s 【13†Gateway Configs】. (others being `fallback` and `loadbalance`). To use it in your app,
L113: 
L114:   1. You need to create a `conditional` config in Portkey UI.
L115:   2. Save the Config and get an associated Config ID.
L116:   3. And just pass the Config ID along with your requests using the `config` param.
L117: ##
L118: 
L119: 【47†​】
L120: 
L121: 1. Creating the `conditional` Config
L122: 
L123: Here’s how a sample `conditional` config looks (along with its simpler, tree view).
L124: 
L125:   * Sample Config
L126:   * Tree View
L127: 
L128:     `{
L129:       "strategy": {
L130:         "mode": "conditional",
L131:         "conditions": [
L132:           ...conditions
L133:         ],
L134:         "default": "target_1"
L135:       },
L136:       "targets": [
L137:         {
L138:           "name": "target_1",
L139:           "provider": "@xx"
L140:         },
L141:         {
L142:           "name": "target_2",
L143:           "provider": "@yy"
L144:         }
L145:       ]
L146:     }
L147:     `
L148: 
L149:     `│─ config
L150:     │  │─ strategy mode:conditional
L151:     │  │  │─ conditions
L152:     │  │  │  │─ array of conditions
L153:     │  │  │─ default
L154:     │  │  │  │─ target name
L155:     │  │─ targets
L156:     │  │  │─ target 1
L157:     │  │  │  │─ name
L158:     │  │  │  │─ provider details
L159:     │  │  │─ target 2
L160:     │  │  │  │─ name
L161:     │  │  │  │─ provider details
L162:     `
L163:   * `strategy.mode`: Set to `conditional`
L164:   * `strategy.conditions`: Query conditions with rules applied on metadata values or request parameters along with which target to call when the condition passes
L165:   * `strategy.default`: The default target name to call when none of the conditions pass
L166:   * `targets`: Array of target objects with unique `names` and provider details. These target names are referenced in the `conditions` objects above.
L167: `conditions` and `default` are required params for the `conditional` strategy.
L168: ###
L169: 
L170: 【48†​】
L171: 
L172: Structure of `conditions` Object
L173: 
L174: `conditions` are where you will actually write the routing rules. Here’s a sample `condition` object:
L175: 
L176:   * Metadata Based
L177: 
L178:   * Params Based
L179: 
L180:     `  {
L181:         "query": { "metadata.user_plan": { "$eq": "paid" } },
L182:         "then": "finetuned-gpt4"
L183:       }
L184:     `
L185: 
L186:     `{
L187:       "query": { "params.model": { "$eq": "smartest" } },
L188:       "then": "smartest-model-target"
L189:     }
L190:     `
L191: `query`: Write the exact rule for checking metadata values or request parameters `then`: Define which target to call if the query `PASSES`
L192: ####
L193: 
L194: 【49†​】
L195: 
L196: Supported Query Paths and Limits
L197:   * `metadata.<key>`: Looks up `context.metadata[<key>]`. Keys must be flat (no additional dots) and values should be primitive types.
L198:   * `params.<key>`: Looks up `context.params[<key>]`. Only primitive values are supported for comparisons.
L199:   * `url.pathname`: Matches against the full request path (for example, `/admin/users`).
L200: Note: Only two-segment keys are supported (for example, `metadata.user_plan`, `params.model`). Nested paths like `metadata.features.new_model_enabled` are not supported.
L201: ###
L202: 
L203: 【50†​】
L204: 
L205: List of Condition Query Operators
L206: 
L207: Operator  | Description
L208: --- | ---
L209: `$eq`  | Equals
L210: `$ne`  | Not equals
L211: `$in`  | In array
L212: `$nin`  | Not in array
L213: `$regex`  | Match the regex
L214: `$gt`  | Greater than
L215: `$gte`  | Greater than or equal to
L216: `$lt`  | Less than
L217: `$lte`  | Less than or equal to
L218: 
L219:   * `$regex` uses JavaScript regular expressions with no flags. Matching is case-sensitive by default, and invalid patterns simply cause the condition to evaluate to `false`.
L220: ###
L221: 
L222: 【51†​】
L223: 
L224: Logical Query Operators
L225: 
L226:   * `$and`: All conditions must be true
L227:   * `$or`: At least one condition must be true
L228: ** Example Condition objects with Logical Operators**
L229: 
L230:   * AND
L231: 
L232:   * OR
L233:   * MIXED Conditions
L234: 
L235:     `{
L236:       "$and": [
L237:         { "metadata.user_type": { "$eq": "pro" } },
L238:         { "metadata.model": { "$eq": "gpt-4" } }
L239:       ]
L240:     }
L241:     `
L242: 
L243:     `{
L244:       "$or": [
L245:         { "params.temperature": { "$gt": 0.7 } },
L246:         { "params.top_p": { "$lt": 0.8 } }
L247:       ]
L248:     }
L249:     `
L250: 
L251:     `{
L252:       "$or": [
L253:         {
L254:           "$and": [
L255:             { "metadata.user_type": { "$eq": "pro" } },
L256:             { "params.model": { "$eq": "gpt-4o" } }
L257:           ]
L258:         },
L259:         { "params.max_tokens": { "$gt": 1000 } }
L260:       ]
L261:     }
L262:     `
L263:   1. You can write nested queries (with `$and`, `$or` operators)
L264:   2. When a condition evaluates to `false` or is malformed, Portkey moves on to the next condition until it finds a successful one.
L265:   3. If no conditions pass, then the `default` target name is called
L266:   4. Since Portkey iterates through the queries sequentially, the order of your conditions is important
L267:   5. If a referenced key is missing (in `metadata`, `params`, or `url`), the condition evaluates to `false`; it does not throw an error.
L268: ##
L269: 
L270: 【52†​】
L271: 
L272: 2. Getting Config ID
L273:

L277: 【54†​】

L279: 3. Implementing Conditional Routing
L280: 
L281: Conditional routing is enabled through Portkey’s 【13†Gateway Configs】 by following these steps:

L287: ## Parameter-Based Routing

L299: Routing Based on Request Parameters

+not require granting Twyne a new named-model scope: it preserves its existing
+`infer:fast`, `infer:balanced`, `infer:reasoning` and `infer:vision` grants.
*** End Patch"));

content.text:
You’re right: **Inkling should handle Twyne’s text-producing intelligence, including image understanding**, rather than being limited to text-only inputs.

That covers editing, research extraction, agent/tool responses, scene-image readings, and voice-action interpretation. Spoken conversations should also use Inkling for the response, with a separate model rendering that response as speech. Twyne’s current GPT Live connection needs a pipeline change to support that separation.

One correction to my earlier answer: **audio input on Inkling 2 Small is not yet verified**. The current catalog lists it as text + vision; the audio documentation explicitly names older Inkling models. We shouldn’t assume that capability carries over. [Model catalog](https://tinker-docs.thinkingmachines.ai/tinker/models/models_and_pricing/), [audio documentation](https://tinker-docs.thinkingmachines.ai/cookbook/inkling/audio/).

I prepared the [Twyne-specific routing patch](/tmp/twyne-inkling-production-20261106/twyne-routing.patch), covering `fast`, `balanced`, `reasoning`, and `vision`. **77 focused tests pass.** Audio and image format compatibility still need verification.

**Production remains unchanged:** the available Portkey credential returns `403 insufficient permissions` for config readback, blocking safe publication.
